subject: L for the last day of the month in the day field
brief:
Let the day-of-month field of a cronlite expression say "the last day of the month" with the letter L, and make every part of the package that reads fields understand it.

1. In the day-of-month field only, an item may be `L` (either letter case) instead of a number, alone or in a comma list next to numbers. The parsed `FieldSpec` gets a new boolean attribute `last` (False unless the field contains L); L adds no number to `values`, and a field containing L is not a wildcard. L in any other field raises CronError whose message starts with that field's name.
2. The expression matches on a day when the day-of-month field holds that day's number or holds L and the day is the last of its month, which depends on the month and, for February, on leap years. Finding the next firing time follows from that. L counts as a restriction of the day of month: when the weekday is also restricted, the classic rule applies and either one matching is enough.
3. `canonical` writes L in upper case after the numbers of the field, so equivalent spellings compare equal and a field with L differs from the same numbers without it; only a field that already lists every day number is still written as a star (the L adds nothing there).
4. `describe` reads the day part as the ordinals of the field's numbers followed by the words "last day", joined like any other list of words, then "of the month" (for example a field of 3 and L reads "on the 3rd and last day of the month"); the either-rule wording with a weekday stays as it is.
5. In `lint`, L exists in every month: it never causes the `never` or `leap-only` warning, and an expression whose day field is only L gets no day warning at all. The numbers next to it are still checked as before, so a number that some chosen month lacks still gives `missing-days`.
6. `duplicates` (and so `lint_all`) must not treat a field with L as the same as the field without it.

All behavior that the existing tests check must keep working.
